title: Where Travel Protection Plans Cover Stands against an Air Ticket Fare Brands Tax Return
content:
Where a traveller has bought cover under the Travel Protection Plans against an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking, part of the figure otherwise returned as carrier-imposed taxes is held back, because the cover has already met some of the traveller's loss. What decides how much is what that cover has actually settled in claims over the last 12 months.

## 1. The shares

| Where | The share returned is |
| --- | --- |
| protection cover bought against this booking is on file and it has settled 400.00 USD or more in claims over the last 12 months | 0.7, being 70 percent |
| protection cover bought against this booking is on file and it has settled less than 400.00 USD in claims over that period | 0.8, being 80 percent |
| in every other case | no such holding back is made |

## 2. What counts as settled

What the cover has settled is read as the sums actually paid out on claims, never as the sums claimed and never as the claims the insurer declined.

## 3. Where the cover is found

The cover in question is a policy under the Travel Protection Plans standing on file against this air booking. The claims read are the claims recorded against that policy, and the sums read are what those claims actually paid out, over the 12 months back from today.

## 4. Boundary readings, on hypothetical figures

A policy that has paid out exactly 400.00 USD in claims inside the window reaches the threshold, so 70 percent of the figure is returned; one that has paid out 399.99 USD falls short of it, and 80 percent is returned.

A policy that stands on file but has paid out nothing inside the window has settled less than 400.00 USD, so 80 percent is returned — the second row, not the third, because the cover is on file.

Where no such cover stands on file at all, no holding back is made.
